faqs.a: A query language for JSON, like XPath for XML. Expressions such as $.store.book[?(@.price < 10)].title select values by navigating the document structure.
$ is the document root. .name selects a child property, [0] the first array item, [-1] the last, [*] all children, and ..name searches recursively at any depth.
[?(...)] keeps only items matching the condition, where @ is the current item: [?(@.price < 10)] keeps books cheaper than 10. You can combine conditions with &&, ||, !, and parentheses.
Yes: [0:2] takes items 0 and 1, [::2] takes every second item, and [0,2] takes items 0 and 2 (a union). Negative indices count from the end.
Use brackets with quotes: $.store['book title'] or $['store']['book']. Dots only work for simple identifier-like names.
faqs.q: How do I access keys with spaces or special characters?

jsonpath-tester.formula:
$.store.book[0].title   -> child, index, child
$.store.book[*].author    -> wildcard over array
$..price                   -> recursive: every 'price' at any depth
$.store.book[0:2]          -> slice: items 0 and 1
$.store.book[0,2]          -> union: items 0 and 2
$.store.book[-1]           -> negative index: last item
$[?(@.price < 10)]         -> filter: @ is the current item
filters: == != < <= > >=, && || !, ( ), @.field, @[0]

keyFacts: JSONPath Tester evaluates JSONPath expressions against any JSON document, live.
$ is the root; .child and ['child'] navigate objects; [0], [-1], and [0:2] navigate arrays.
* selects all children; ..name searches recursively for a key at any depth.
[?(@.price < 10)] filters arrays with comparisons, &&, ||, !, and parentheses.
[0,2] is a union selecting multiple indices; negative indices count from the end.
Every match reports its full path (like $.store.book[2].title) and its value.
jsonpath-tester.keywords: jsonpath tester, jsonpath online, test jsonpath expression, jsonpath query tool, jsonpath evaluator
limitations: Covers the practical core only: script expressions and regex match operators are not supported.
Recursive descent (..) on huge documents may be slow since it walks the whole tree.
Filter errors are treated as non-matches rather than reported - keep expressions simple.
Path display uses bracket notation for unusual keys, which some JSONPath flavors write differently.

jsonpath-tester.workedExample:
Document: a store with 4 books priced 8.95, 12.99, 8.99, 22.99.

Expression: $.store.book[?(@.price < 10)].title
1. $.store.book selects the array of 4 books.
2. [?(@.price < 10)] keeps books 0 and 2 (8.95 and 8.99).
3. .title extracts the title of each.

Result - 2 matches:
$.store.book[0].title = "Sayings of the Century"
$.store.book[2].title = "Moby Dick"
